item.title: Zanu PF councillor ordered to repay vendors after fraud conviction
item.description: Zanu-PF Ward 1 councillor, Josiah Mutangi, who was convicted of 13 counts of fraud for duping vendors of their money, has been ordered to perform 490 hours of community service at Bulawayo Central Police Station, and to restitute the victims their money by February 27, 2026.

item.title: Nkulumane resident confronts Zanu PF candidate over 2030 push
item.description: Tensions flared at the Meet Your Candidates town hall debate in Nkulumane on Wednesday when a female attendee confronted Zanu PF’s parliamentary candidate, Freedom Murechu, demanding to know how he intended to “save the constitution” amid a plan by the ruling party to extend the presidential term to 2030 and possibly postpone the 2028 elections.

item.title: Zimbabwe Bars Foreigners from Certain Businesses, Reserve Sectors for Locals
item.description: Zimbabwe has introduced new regulations restricting the participation of foreign nationals in seventeen economic sectors and sub-sectors that are reserved for local citizens.

item.title: Tungwarara’s Central Committee Co-Option Heads To Politburo
item.description: ZANU PF spokesperson Christopher Mutsvangwa says the issue of Paul Tungwarara’s co-option into the party’s Central Committee will be handled by the Politburo, just as it dealt with Kudakwashe Tagwirei’s co-option by the Harare Province.

item.title: Parents of stranded SA team players in Zimbabwe demand accountability from Chess SA
item.description: South African youth players and their parents were left stranded in Zimbabwe at the African Youth Chess Championship after Chess South Africa failed to pay their accommodation fees on time.

item.title: Does Trump Matter?
item.description: This question is being asked across the globe. Here in Africa the issue is of little consequence except that the aid provided by USAID has stopped, thousands face starvation and the programs that have helped the poor survive in many countries is no longer available.
